Buffer of Thoughts (BoT)

A novel framework that boosts accuracy, efficiency, and robustness by retrieving thought templates from a "Meta-Buffer".

The Concept

Buffer of Thoughts (BoT) moves away from generating reasoning steps from scratch every time. Instead, it maintains a library (buffer) of high-level thought templates or "reasoning structures" distilled from previous successful problem-solving. When a new problem arrives, BoT retrieves a relevant thought-template and instantiates it with specific problem details.

Why BoT?

  • Efficiency: Reduces token usage by using compact templates rather than verbose verbose CoT generation.
  • Robustness: Templates acts as "skeletons" that guide the model, reducing hallucination in the reasoning logic itself.
  • Generalization: A single template (e.g., "Divide and Conquer") can solve many different types of math problems.

BoT Workflow

  1. Problem Distiller: Extracts key parameters and constraints from the query.
  2. Template Retrieval: Finds the most similar "Thought Template" from the Meta-Buffer.
  3. Instantiation: The LLM fills in the specific variables of the template.
  4. Execution: The instantiated thought structure is executed to get the answer.
